what: Calculate a location quotient / distinctive risk ratio — risk_calc_location_quotient
title: Calculate a location quotient / distinctive risk ratio — risk_calc_location_quotient
text: Calculates location quotient local rate divided reference rate. follows general approach used Boscoe Pradhan (2015), mapped distinctive cause death comparing state-specific age-adjusted mortality rates national age-adjusted mortality rates.

title: Calculate a location quotient / distinctive risk ratio — risk_calc_location_quotient
code: risk_calc_location_quotient(   data,   observed_col = "event_count",   denominator_col,   reference_rate = NULL,   lq_col = "location_quotient",   local_rate_col = "local_rate",   min_count = 0 )

title: Calculate a location quotient / distinctive risk ratio — risk_calc_location_quotient
text: data data frame sf object. observed_col Column containing observed counts. denominator_col Column containing population, exposure, denominator. reference_rate Optional fixed reference rate. NULL, reference rate calculated rows. lq_col Name output location quotient column. local_rate_col Name local rate output column. min_count Minimum observed count required calculating LQ.

title: Calculate a location quotient / distinctive risk ratio — risk_calc_location_quotient
text: Input data local rate location quotient columns.

title: Calculate a location quotient / distinctive risk ratio — risk_calc_location_quotient
text: Boscoe FP, Pradhan E. Distinctive Causes Death State, 2001–2010. Preventing Chronic Disease. 2015;12:E75. doi:10.5888/pcd12.140395.

title: Calculate a location quotient / distinctive risk ratio — risk_calc_location_quotient
code: data <- data.frame(   event_count = c(5, 10, 20),   population = c(1000, 2000, 3000) )  risk_calc_location_quotient(   data = data,   observed_col = "event_count",   denominator_col = "population" ) #>   event_count population  local_rate location_quotient #> 1           5       1000 0.005000000         0.8571429 #> 2          10       2000 0.005000000         0.8571429 #> 3          20       3000 0.006666667         1.1428571

title: Calculate Poisson probability of one or more events — risk_calc_poisson_probability
text: implementation uses observed historical event frequency derive Poisson lambda value: $$ P(X \geq 1) = 1 - e^{-\lambda} $$ \(\lambda\) average event count target period.
